title: Chicken Porkolt
subtitle: Hungarian braised chicken in rich paprika onion sauce
excerpt: Bone-in chicken thighs slow-braised in a thick sauce of onion, sweet paprika, and tomato until deeply tender. Served with egg noodles or boiled potatoes to catch the sauce.
sourceNotes: Hungarian porkolt tradition, a close relative of goulash. Synthesised from multiple Hungarian culinary sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked dish without the egg noodles. Reheat gently on the hob, adding a splash of water if needed.
recipe.batchNotes: Easily doubled. The flavour improves the next day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook a day ahead and refrigerate. The sauce deepens in flavour overnight.

content.text: Porkolt is built on one principle: cook the onions until they melt, then add paprika off the heat so it blooms without burning. The chicken braises slowly in almost no liquid. Use good sweet paprika as it is the defining flavour of the dish.

items.prepNote: use the best quality you have

content.text: Heat the oil in the dutch oven over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 15 minutes until golden and soft.
Take the pan off the heat. Add the paprika-sweet and paprika-hot. Stir quickly to coat the onions. Return to a low heat.
Add the garlic, tomato, and green pepper. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces and stir to coat in the onion and paprika base. Season with salt and black pepper.
Pour over the stock. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot and cook on a low heat for 40 minutes until the chicken is very tender and the sauce is thick.
Remove the lid and cook for a further 5 minutes if the sauce needs thickening. Taste and adjust the salt.
Cook the tagliatelle according to the packet instructions. Serve the porkolt over the noodles with a spoonful of soured cream and parsley on top.

items.cause: The paprika was added to a hot pan and scorched.
items.fix: Always take the pan off the heat before adding paprika. It should never fry in hot fat.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: Too much stock was added, or the lid was on throughout.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer on a medium heat for 10 minutes to reduce. The onion base will help it thicken naturally.

items.cause: It cooked too fast on too high a heat.
items.fix: Keep the heat at the lowest possible simmer. The chicken should bubble gently rather than boil hard.
